chapter: Fletcher Henderson, Ella Fitzgerald and the early 1940s
title: Leading Ella Fitzgerald's orchestra, 1940-42
summary: He got the job conducting Ella's band from Savoy owner Charlie Buchanan, ran rehearsals, enlarged the band and toured to California. The last job in 1942 was in Philadelphia with Bill Robinson before he went to ABC.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: And I come back and I worked with Don Redman in that era somewhere. Then finally one day I was down back of the Apollo Theater and I ran into Charlie Buchanan who had the Savoy. And he said, well, when are you going to come back and work for me. I said, well, I don't want to come back up there but if you want me to do something get me the job conducting for Ella. So he did. He said, meet me down to the office tomorrow. And I went down and (unintelligible) and talked to them and they gave me the job leading the band. So I had to go to Boston and hear the band and everything and then we brought the band back into New York and rehearsed for a couple of weeks.
Well, did she stand in front of the band?
She just would sit down like --
Right. And I used to -- I ran the whole thing. She sang whatever I called for her to sing and

I made arrangements for her and me and Dick Vance and a few others made arrangements. And we took a trip after I got the band in shape because I added on some more men, different things, enlarged the band a little bit. I had three -- instead of the regular three trumpets and two trombones I had three trombones and four trumpets and five saxes. And then we took a trip out West, Grand Terrace and all, went all the way to California and back. And this brought us back to around 1941.
Well, '42, rather. And our last job we played was in the Earl Theater in Philadelphia with Bill Robinson.
Yeah. Then I left there and came into New York and went to work at ABC.
